decisions.reason: The NL phrase 'When the UAV swarm is intercepted' is genuinely ambiguous between two competent readings: (1) 'when the interception event is detected while in the Searching state' requiring a direct Searching→FormationAdjustment edge (absent, confirmed by S2=false and complete inventory), and (2) 'when the swarm is in the intercepted condition (the Intercepted state)' which is satisfied by the existing Intercepted→FormationAdjustment edge (transition:line:26). The linguistic form 'is intercepted' (passive stative) more naturally describes a state/condition than an event moment. The model's two-step path Searching→Intercepted→FormationAdjustment achieves the behavioral outcome under reading (2). Both readings are compatible with the supplied NL and model facts, so the violation is established under the primary contract reading but a competent alternative reading remains.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL3 requires that when the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state; the primary reading binds the source to the Searching operating state and requires a direct Searching→FormationAdjustment edge, which is absent from the closed model inventory.

decisions.reason: The NL states 'continuously performs target search tasks' which in formal UML/FCSTM semantics requires a do activity. The FCSTM Searching state has no do, entry, or exit action (S4=false, abstract_action_inventory=0). However, the PlantUML source (line 4) includes the annotation 'Searching : Target Search Task' as a state body description. In some modeling conventions, a state's descriptive annotation implies its ongoing activity without requiring an explicit do keyword. This creates two competent readings: (1) a formal do action is required (violated), and (2) the state description annotation suffices as a conventional representation of the ongoing activity (satisfied). Both readings are compatible with the supplied facts.

The intermediate Intercepted state is a legitimate modeling refinement that preserves the behavioral outcome without requiring a direct edge.
issues.title: Missing direct edge from Searching to FormationAdjustment on interception

issues.basis: NL2: 'the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks'; contract binding hints state=Searching, phase=do, action='perform target search tasks'; FCSTM state:Searching:line:19 has no action fields; reference inspection facts metrics.abstract_action_inventory=[]; source PlantUML line 4 shows 'Searching : Target Search Task' as a body label only.
issues.expected: The Searching state has a do action representing continuous performance of target search tasks.
locus_names: UAV swarm target search operating state
issues.observed: The FCSTM Searching state (state:Searching:line:19) has no do action. Its name includes the PlantUML body annotation 'Target Search Task' but no formal do clause. The reference inspection facts show abstract_action_inventory count is 0 across the entire model. No action is declared on any state.
issues.reason: The contract requires a do-phase action 'perform target search tasks' on the Searching state. The complete FCSTM model declares zero abstract actions (inspection metric abstract_action_inventory count=0). The Searching state has no entry, do, or exit actions. The state description in its name is not a formal do action in FCSTM semantics.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML state body 'Searching : Target Search Task' could be interpreted as describing the ongoing activity of the state, and the state's outgoing transitions (to Intercepted and Attack) imply it is an active operating state. The absence of a formal do clause may be a modeling convention rather than a semantic omission.
issues.title: Missing do action for target search on Searching state

issues.basis: NL4: 'After completing the attack, the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly'; FCSTM variable declaration 'def int R45RouteToken = 0'; transition:line:17 effect 'R45RouteToken = 7'; transition:line:22 guard 'R45RouteToken == 7' effect 'R45RouteToken = 0'; source inventory events include 'Attack Complete' but no variable declarations; canonical IR variables count=0.
issues.expected: After the attack state is completed (exit via Attack_Complete), a variable representing the number of UAVs in the swarm is decreased.
locus_names: number of UAVs in the swarm
issues.observed: The FCSTM declares only one variable: R45RouteToken (a route control token). The attack completion transition (AttackingTarget→[*], transition:line:17) has effect 'R45RouteToken = 7'. The follow-up transition (Attack→Searching, transition:line:22) has guard 'R45RouteToken == 7' and effect 'R45RouteToken = 0'. No variable represents UAV count, and no effect decreases such a variable.
issues.reason: The contract requires a variable_delta property: after attack completion, the 'number of UAVs in the swarm' must decrease. The closed model contains no variable with this semantic meaning. The only variable (R45RouteToken) serves as a routing mechanism between composite exit and parent-level return transitions. The required variable is absent and no effect on any existing variable represents a UAV count decrease. No frozen predicate directly expresses variable_delta semantics, so predicate_id is null.
issues.requirement_quote: After completing the attack, the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The R45RouteToken variable may encode swarm composition information indirectly, and the value 7 set on attack completion could represent a reduced count. However, this is speculative; the variable name and usage pattern (set to 5 on adjustment, 7 on attack, 0 on return) indicate it is a routing token, not a UAV counter.
issues.title: No variable representing UAV swarm count; attack completion effect is route token only

issues.basis: NL2: 'Before the mission is completed' establishes mission completion as a bounding condition; canonical_source_ir.model.final_states=[]; FCSTM transition topology: all exits from FormationAdjustment and Attack return to Searching (lines 21, 22); no transition targets a final/terminal state; verify_facts terminal_state='completed' refers to the verification check status, not a model state.
issues.expected: A mission completion or terminal state exists and is reachable, providing the bound beyond which target search operations cease.
issues.observed: The canonical source IR lists final_states as an empty array. The FCSTM contains no terminal/final state. The model's topology creates cycles: Searching↔FormationAdjustment (via Intercepted) and Searching↔Attack (via AttackingTarget). All return paths go back to Searching, with no exit to a completion state. The mission cannot terminate.
issues.reason: The contract establishes that the UAV swarm mission must reach completion (termination_state role). The NL explicitly bounds target search operations by mission completion ('Before the mission is completed...'), implying a completion state exists. The closed model has no final states (canonical final_states=[]) and all transitions cycle back to Searching. No path leads to a terminal state. No frozen predicate directly expresses the existence-and-reachability of a terminal state, so predicate_id is null.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL phrase 'before the mission is completed' may be a temporal bounding condition rather than a requirement for an explicit terminal state in this particular state machine diagram. The mission completion might be modeled externally or in a higher-level system. However, the state machine as specified has no mechanism for ceasing operations.
issues.title: No mission completion or terminal state exists in the model

issues.basis: FCSTM transition:line:28 ([*]→UnspecifiedInitial in root scope); state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:7 (is_composite=false, outgoing_transition_refs=[]); verify fact reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:8 status=refuted; inspection diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for all 7 descendant states; working contract compiler_owned synthetic_state for UnspecifiedInitial; source tr_0001 confirms author intended UAVSwarmStateMachine as the entry scope.
issues.expected: A path exists from the root machine's initial state to UAVSwarmStateMachine, enabling entry into the operating scope where all described swarm behavior occurs.
issues.observed: The root initial edge (transition:line:28) targets UnspecifiedInitial, a synthetic compiler-owned leaf state with no outgoing transitions. No edge exists from the root or from UnspecifiedInitial into UAVSwarmStateMachine. Verify facts confirm reachability of UAVSwarmStateMachine from initial is refuted. All 7 states inside UAVSwarmStateMachine are unreachable. All 4 event consumers are unreachable. The only reachable states are the root wrapper and UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: The NL establishes UAVSwarmStateMachine as the operating scope for all described behavior. For any obligation to be executable, this scope must be reachable from the machine's initial state. The FCSTM root initial targets a dead synthetic state instead. This is an independent root-entry structural defect that prevents all downstream behavior from executing, distinct from the internal endpoint/action/termination issues.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The UnspecifiedInitial state and its incoming root edge are compiler-owned synthetic artifacts (working contract element_id compiler:state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0006.UnspecifiedInitial, kind=synthetic_state). The source model's initial pseudostate edge (tr_0001: [*]→Searching within UAVSwarmStateMachine) correctly appears in FCSTM as transition:line:23. The root-level entry defect may be a lowering artifact rather than an author error, and the internal structure of UAVSwarmStateMachine is faithfully preserved.
issues.title: UAVSwarmStateMachine unreachable from root initial; entire operating scope dead

issues.basis: FCSTM transition:line:28 (root[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial); UnspecifiedInitial has outgoing_transition_refs=[] (deadlock leaf, synthetic); verify_facts non_proved reachability:state:UAVSwarmStateMachine:line:8 status=refuted; inspection_equivalent_facts reachable_state_refs contains only root and UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.expected: The UAVSwarmStateMachine composite (operating scope containing all target search states) must be reachable from the root initial entry so that the swarm can begin its mission operations.
issues.observed: The root's only initial transition (transition:line:28) targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state which has no outgoing transitions. UAVSwarmStateMachine has no incoming transition from the root level. verify_facts confirm reachability is refuted: reachable_from_initial=false for all 7 states within UAVSwarmStateMachine.
issues.reason: The root reachability of the operating scope is a necessary precondition for all NL2/NL3/NL4 behavioral obligations. Without it, no target search, interception response, or task assignment can ever occur. The verify_facts provide a deterministic refutation of the path from root to UAVSwarmStateMachine.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The UAVSwarmStateMachine has its own internal initial entry ([*] -> Searching, transition:line:23, proven by verify_facts), so if the composite were entered, its internal behavior would be well-defined. The issue is solely the missing root-level entry into the composite, not an internal structural defect.
issues.title: UAVSwarmStateMachine operating scope is unreachable from model root initial entry

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers: all 4 entries show non-empty consumer_transition_refs but empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs; verify_facts non_proved: event-consumer:Interception_Detected, event-consumer:Task_Assignment_Received, event-consumer:Adjustment_Complete, event-consumer:Attack_Complete all status=refuted; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for all 4 events.
issues.expected: Each event declared within the UAVSwarmStateMachine operating scope must have at least one consumer transition reachable from the model root initial entry, so that event-driven responses (interception, task assignment, adjustment completion, attack completion) can be operationally triggered.
issues.observed: All four events (Interception_Detected, Task_Assignment_Received, Adjustment_Complete, Attack_Complete) have exactly one declared consumer transition each, but inspection_equivalent_facts confirm reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty for all four. verify_facts refuted all four event-consumer checks. The root cause is that the consumer states (Searching, AdjustingFormation, AttackingTarget) are all unreachable from the root initial entry.
issues.reason: Event consumer coverage is an independent frontier property from root reachability per the cross-view discipline. Even though the root cause is the same (UAVSwarmStateMachine unreachable), the operational consequence is that no event can be consumed, which is a distinct behavioral failure from the scope being unreachable. This contract captures the event-level operational deadness.
issues.requirement_quote: When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The events and their consumers are correctly declared and structurally connected within UAVSwarmStateMachine. If the root reachability issue were fixed, all four events would have exactly one reachable consumer each. The coverage failure is entirely downstream of the root reachability defect.
issues.title: All four declared events have no reachable consumer within the operating scope

issues.basis: NL2 text 'Before the mission is completed' establishes termination bound; canonical_source_ir.final_states=[]; PlantUML source has no UAVSwarmStateMachine --> [*] edge; source_inventory transitions show all exits from sub-states route to Searching (tr_0005, tr_0007), not to any terminal; verify_facts confirm no reachable final state exists.
issues.expected: The UAV swarm mission must have a completion/termination state that is reachable from the operating scope, because NL2 explicitly bounds target search by 'before the mission is completed,' establishing that a mission-complete termination is required.
issues.observed: The canonical_source_ir shows final_states=[] (no final states authored). The PlantUML source has no top-level [*] exit from UAVSwarmStateMachine. All sub-state exits (AdjustingFormation, AttackingTarget) route back to Searching (continued operation), not to any terminal state. Additionally, the entire operating scope is unreachable from the root, so even a hypothetical termination state within it could not be reached.
issues.reason: The termination contract requires that the mission can reach completion. Two independent facts violate this: (1) no terminal/final state exists anywhere in the model hierarchy, and (2) the operating scope itself is unreachable so no path to any potential termination could exist. The absence of any final state in both the PlantUML source and the FCSTM model is a precise structural gap against the NL2 termination bound.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL2 phrase 'before the mission is completed' could be read as a temporal bound on the described behavior rather than an obligation that a termination state must exist in the model. However, the derived contract explicitly interprets it as establishing mission completion as a required reachable property, and no alternative terminal state exists in the source or model.
issues.title: No mission completion or termination state exists in the model

issues.basis: NL4 text 'the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly'; FCSTM declares only variable R45RouteToken (line 1); transition:line:17 effect is 'R45RouteToken = 7'; transition:line:22 effect is 'R45RouteToken = 0'; no other variables or effects exist in the model; PlantUML source has no variable declarations.
issues.expected: After the attack state completes (AttackingTarget exits on Attack_Complete), an effect must decrease a variable representing the number of UAVs in the swarm, reflecting attrition or loss during the attack.
locus_names: number of UAVs in the swarm
issues.observed: The only variable in the model is R45RouteToken (integer, initial value 0), which serves as a route control token. The Attack_Complete transition (transition:line:17) sets R45RouteToken=7, and the subsequent Attack->Searching transition (transition:line:22) resets it to 0. No variable tracks UAV count, and no effect decreases such a variable. The PlantUML source has no variable declarations at all.
issues.reason: NL4 explicitly requires that 'the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases' after attack completion. The model has no variable with this semantic role and no effect that produces a decrease in any count-like variable. The R45RouteToken effects are route-control assignments, not population deltas. This is a precise behavioral gap: the post-attack composition update is entirely absent from the model.
issues.requirement_quote: After completing the attack, the number of UAVs in the swarm decreases accordingly.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: R45RouteToken could be interpreted as an encoding of swarm composition state (value 7 might represent a specific UAV count configuration). However, the variable name, its usage pattern (set to 5 or 7 as route tokens, reset to 0), and its role as a guard for sub-state-to-parent exits make it a route control mechanism, not a UAV count tracker. No monotonic decrease semantics are present.
issues.title: No variable representing UAV swarm count exists and no decrease effect is defined after attack completion

issues.basis: NL2 text 'continuously performs target search tasks'; PlantUML line 5 'Searching : Target Search Task' (note syntax, not do syntax); FCSTM state:Searching:line:19 has no action fields; reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory count=0; source_trace body:UAVSwarmStateMachine.Searching:4 maps the annotation to a body projection, not an action.
issues.expected: The Searching state (UAV swarm target search operating state) must have a do lifecycle action representing the continuous performance of target search tasks, as NL2 requires continuous operation during the search phase.
locus_names: UAV swarm target search operating state
issues.observed: The FCSTM Searching state (state:Searching:line:19) has no do, entry, or exit action. The PlantUML annotation 'Searching : Target Search Task' (line 5) is a state description/note, not a UML do activity. In the FCSTM, this text is embedded in the state's name string but is not represented as an executable lifecycle action. The reference_inspection_facts show abstract_action_inventory is empty (count=0).
issues.reason: NL2 requires the swarm to 'continuously perform target search tasks' during operation. In state machine semantics, continuous behavior during a state is represented by a do activity. The FCSTM has no do action on Searching, and the PlantUML annotation is a descriptive note rather than a formal do activity. The abstract_action_inventory being empty confirms no actions are defined anywhere in the model. This is a missing behavioral representation: the continuous search activity is not executable in the closed model.
issues.requirement_quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML state annotation 'Target Search Task' could be interpreted as implicitly representing the ongoing activity of the state, even without an explicit do keyword. In some UML conventions, a state's name or description implies its activity. However, the FCSTM formalism requires explicit action declarations for executable behavior, and none is present.
issues.title: No do action representing continuous target search is defined on the Searching state

decisions.reason: NL3 states 'When the UAV swarm is intercepted, it transitions to the formation adjustment state.' The primary binding resolves 'UAV swarm operating state' to Searching and 'formation adjustment state' to FormationAdjustment, requiring a direct edge between them. The complete closed transition inventory (11 edges) contains no Searching to FormationAdjustment edge. The interception event (Interception_Detected) on Searching targets Intercepted (transition:line:24), and a separate untriggered edge Intercepted to FormationAdjustment exists (transition:line:26). The strongest alternative reading is that 'when the UAV swarm is intercepted' names the Intercepted state as the source, in which case transition:line:26 satisfies the contract. Both readings are compatible with the NL text: the phrase can describe either the event condition (requiring the direct edge) or the resulting state (satisfied by the two-step path). The exact facts establish the primary reading is violated, and the alternative is a competent surviving undercutting defeater.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The NL phrase 'when the UAV swarm is intercepted' may identify the Intercepted state as the transition source rather than Searching; under that reading, the existing edge Intercepted to FormationAdjustment (transition:line:26) satisfies the requirement, and the two-step path is a legitimate modeling refinement that preserves the behavioral outcome.

The exact absence of the do action is established, and the annotation-based reading is a competent surviving undercutting defeater.
